summary: The current design has several execution, identity, and validation gaps that can prevent the research pass from running or make its audit trail unreliable. The largest risks are undefined invocation inputs, unsupported defaults, hotfix handling, stale staging, and tests that validate presence rather than behavior.

suggestions.title: Make brief rendering executable
suggestions.rationale: The documented Python renderer references undefined variables, and `$REPO_ROOT` is never initialized in either command twin. A literal run therefore fails before Codex starts; use a checked-in renderer or explicitly bind every value and the repository root.

suggestions.title: Align the research model with supported configuration
suggestions.rationale: The research command defaults to `gpt-5.6-luna`, while the existing Codex configuration and catalog default to `gpt-5.5` and advertise only `gpt-5.5` variants. Because probe failure becomes a skip, the new feature can be disabled by default despite an installed Codex CLI.

suggestions.title: Define transcript identity for hotfix specs
suggestions.rationale: The spec flow explicitly supports hotfixes without a FEAT ID, but research persistence and the template require `sdd/state/<FEAT-ID>/design_research/`. A hotfix research run has no valid destination; use a shared identity rule such as Jira key or slug.

suggestions.title: Use unique and atomic research staging
suggestions.rationale: Staging is keyed only by feature name with `mkdir -p`, and the repository already ignores the staging tree. A rerun can consume stale `suggestions.json` or mix artifacts before the final `mv *`; use a unique run directory, a manifest, and atomic promotion with cleanup on failure.

suggestions.title: Enforce repository containment for paths
suggestions.rationale: The prompt requires repo-relative paths, but validation only performs `test -e`, and the schema accepts arbitrary strings. Absolute paths, traversal, or symlinks could cause the reviewer or triage step to read outside the repository; resolve and reject paths outside the Codex root.

suggestions.title: Implement the claimed background lifecycle
suggestions.rationale: The documented Codex invocation has no background operator or PID join, despite instructing the agent to continue codebase research while it runs. Either define a real background/wait protocol with timeout and exit capture, or remove the claim and document that `/sdd-spec` waits up to 600 seconds.

suggestions.title: Test the complete skip-and-promote state machine
suggestions.rationale: Current tests validate template placeholders, a sample schema payload, and section presence, but do not execute rendering, probe failure, timeout, invalid JSON, triage, transcript promotion, or hotfix identity. Add fake-Codex subprocess tests covering each non-blocking branch.

suggestions.title: Make twin parity fail closed
suggestions.rationale: The parity test removes any line beginning with `- Worktree policy:` and any line containing a broad sub-feature phrase, allowing future substantive drift to be hidden. Assert exactly the documented frontmatter and exact per-file substitutions instead of broad normalization.

suggestions.title: Factor shared Codex invocation policy
suggestions.rationale: The raw shell protocol duplicates model, sandbox, timeout, output-schema, and repository-boundary policy already represented by `CodexCodeDispatcher`, its profiles, and command-shape tests. A small checked-in helper could share safe argument construction without coupling slash commands to Redis/event dispatch.

suggestions.title: Validate blueprint substance, not headings
suggestions.rationale: The task template permits generic placeholder imports, `NotImplementedError`, and unbounded generated content, while tests only check that an Implementation Blueprint heading exists. Add checks that generated tasks cover every declared file, contain no template placeholders, and bound each `FILL IN` decision to a constraint or acceptance criterion.
